title: Nevetek, Nevettem: Laughing at a Joke

sections.title: A regular verb, plus one case you already know
sections.content: nevet ("to laugh") is a fully regular verb, so it follows exactly the pattern you already know: nevetek, nevetsz, nevet... in the present, and nevettem, nevettél, nevetett... in the past — no stem changes at all. To say what you're laughing AT, Hungarian reaches for the same superessive case (-n/-on/-en/-ön) you already use for locations: nevetünk a viccen ("we laugh at the joke"), not a separate word for "at".

items.spanish: Tegnap este sokat nevettünk Károly viccén.
items.english: Last night we laughed a lot at Károly's joke.

items.spanish: Nevettem a viccén, aztán elmeséltem Károlynak is.
items.english: I laughed at his joke, then told Károly about it too.

items.spanish: Petra elmesélt egy vicces történetet, és mi nagyon nevettünk.
items.english: Petra told a funny story, and we laughed a lot.

sections.content: vicces ("funny") and nevetséges ("ridiculous") both come from a noun plus a descriptive suffix — vicc + -es, nevetség + -es — so once you spot the pattern, new -s/-es/-os/-as adjectives get easier to guess.
